title: Investigate deferred-free buildup and fragmentation in KV cache during continuous batching
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Intermittent GPU memory growth observed on continuous batching workloads that hold long-lived KV caches. Memory does not return to baseline between requests and cumulative usage eventually exhausts capacity on some instances. Symptoms resemble deferred-free buildup in CUDA allocator (cudaMallocAsync) combined with fragmentation from slab pool usage and variable tensor lifetimes from KV cache hits/evictions.
reproduction_steps:
1) Deploy inference runtime build nightlies/runtime-2026-02-20 with continuous batching enabled and KV cache pinned for multi-turn sessions.
2) Run the long-run stress harness (tools/stress/cont_batch_kv.py) with 200 concurrent sessions for 6 hours using sequence lengths sampled from production distribution.
3) Monitor prometheus metrics gpu_mem_total, gpu_mem_free, allocator_pending_bytes, kv_cache_entries, and continuous_batch_queue_depth.
4) Observe steady increase in allocator_pending_bytes and drop in gpu_mem_free after ~90 minutes.
5) Collect pprof heap traces and cudaMallocAsync backlog using CUDA mem usage tracer and nvprof snapshots at 30-minute intervals.
observed_behavior:
- allocator_pending_bytes grows steadily instead of oscillating.
- nvprof shows many outstanding deferred frees on non-default stream.
- Slab pool fragmentation increases: many small free chunks interleaved with large allocated tensors.
- Occasional OOM in high-concurrency tests after ~4–8 hours.
- KV cache eviction rate spikes just before OOM, but freeable memory does not immediately return to global free pool.
expected_behavior: CUDA deferred frees should be reclaimed by the allocator quickly once their associated streams complete, slab pool should coalesce free spans and return memory to the device-level allocator, and KV cache evictions should free memory promptly so long-running batchers remain stable.
investigation_notes:
- Reproduced locally with modified stress harness that increases sequence lengths; observed same pattern.
- Heap snapshots show thousands of small allocations pinned by 'kv_cache_entry' tensors that were logically evicted but not physically freed until stream sync.
- Kernel traces indicate background inferencing streams are different from deallocating/freeing streams; deferred frees are queued on default stream and only processed when that stream synchronizes.
- cudaMallocAsync internal backlog (reported by CUDA debug logs) grows when frees are issued from many worker threads without proper stream association.
- Slab allocator (slab_pool_v2) keeps sub-arenas per-thread; fragmentation arises when mixed-size KV tensors are allocated and freed across different threads leading to many small unusable holes.
root_cause_hypothesis: Combination of three factors: (1) KV cache eviction path issues where frees are enqueued on non-draining streams causing deferred-free backlog; (2) per-thread slab arenas preventing cross-thread coalescing and leading to internal fragmentation; (3) continuous batching keeps old KV tensors alive longer in some code paths so the allocator cannot reuse freed regions quickly. The interplay produces apparent memory leaks even though logical frees occurred.
mitigation_proposed:
Short term: introduce explicit stream-aware deallocation for KV cache evictions (use the compute stream for free or schedule cudaStreamAddCallback to ensure timely processing) and add a periodic forced sync on the default/free stream in the eviction path to drain deferred frees. Also add a background slab compaction job that merges small free spans across sub-arenas at low-priority intervals.
Medium term: audit allocator usage paths to ensure frees include stream handles; change slab_pool to permit cross-thread returns or a global garbage queue to reduce fragmentation. Consider adding an adaptive threshold that disables per-thread arenas when fragmentation metrics exceed a threshold.
Long term: upstream patterns for allocator tuning and recommend SDK guidance to customers about stream-affinity for frees and KV cache sizing heuristics.
immediate_workaround: Disable deferred frees by falling back to cudaFree for KV cache eviction in critical clusters (config flag runtime.disable_deferred_free_for_kv=true). This increases short-term CPU stalls but prevents uncontrolled GPU memory growth until proper fix ships.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Stress harness runs for 24h with 200 concurrent sessions without net increase in allocator_pending_bytes beyond baseline noise.
2) Prometheus alert for allocator_pending_bytes > 50MB sustained is never triggered.
3) Heap snapshots after 24h show no backlog of KV-evicted tensors pending free.
4) Integration tests exercise mixed-thread frees and show successful coalescing of slab spans.
5) Change passes performance regression gate (p99 latency +/-5%).
test_plan:
- Unit tests for KV eviction to assert stream is passed to free path.
- Microbenchmark that allocates/frees many KV-entry-sized tensors from multiple threads to validate no growth.
- Long-run stress in staging for 24h with identical load to reproduction steps.
- Add new prometheus metrics: allocator_free_ops, allocator_deferred_free_backlog, slab_fragmentation_ratio.
- Post-merge run of nightly cluster for 48h to verify rolling pools do not OOM.
comments:
2026-02-26 - Aisha Kapoor: Initial triage — reproducer and metrics collected. Suspect cudaMallocAsync deferred frees interacting poorly with our slab pool.
2026-03-01 - Liam O'Connor: Added micro-reproducer that isolates KV eviction path. Observed that frees issued on helper threads were not associated with the compute stream. Patch candidate created to thread-through stream handles.
2026-03-07 - Maria Chen (SRE): Noted customer cluster CL-42 hit OOM during migration. Applied temporary config runtime.disable_deferred_free_for_kv=true which stabilized the node. We should land short-term workaround quickly.
2026-03-10 - Oliver Brooks (Perf): Ran p99 latency tests on patch branch. No meaningful latency regression (avg +1.2%), but CPU throughput drops ~4% due to forced syncs — acceptable for P0 stability fix.
2026-03-13 - Designated reviewer (PR #1624): Request for additional unit tests covering multi-threaded frees and a metrics-only flag to avoid silent behavioral change in dev mode.
